acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether internal/worksource and internal/contextindex Git runners adopt groupreap.Wait (signal the group before reaping the leader) or keep reaping first, and the decision states how VPO-V0-010 and WQO-V0-005/015/032 treat a descendant that holds the output pipe.
If they adopt it, those requirements and their tests are amended in the same change; if not, the rationale is recorded next to the runner.
body: From the V1-0373 group-reap change on claude/rc1-git-runner-hardening (5cd9419a). groupreap.Wait (internal/groupreap/groupreap_unix.go) waits for the leader with waitid WNOWAIT, SIGKILLs the process group, then reaps. It is adopted by gokernel, doccompiler, cem/gitrun, releasegate, taskman and liveverify/mutate. internal/worksource/process_unix.go (Setpgid) and internal/contextindex Git execution are not adopters: their specs treat a descendant that still holds the output pipe after the leader exits as incomplete output (VPO-V0-010, WQO-V0-005, WQO-V0-015, WQO-V0-032), and a pre-reap kill would close that pipe and change the outcome. Owner question: should these two runners move onto the same order, with the requirements amended, or keep reap-first with the reason stated? Related behaviour change in the adopters: when the leader has exited but a descendant holds stdout, they now return the leader's status instead of ErrWaitDelay or a timeout.
title: Should worksource and contextindex Git runners signal the group before reaping, like groupreap adopters?
